newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark buys German Talkline.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark buys German Talkline.

text.p: Danish telecommuncations group Tele Danmark said on Wednesday it acquired Germany's Talkline mobile telephone company from RWE Telliance for approximately 2.2 billion Danish crowns ($331 million).

"The purchase price of around 2.170 billion crowns, corresponding to approximately 570 million marks or $330 million reflects (Talkline's) strong market position and growth potential as well as the quality of its current customer base," Tele Danmark said in a statement.
On June 13, Tele Danmark announced that it was seeking to buy the mobile telephone company and was close to reaching a deal with RWE Telliance.

Talkline, which operates in Germany, the Netherlands, France and Belgium, was a subsidiary of German industrial group RWE, which is already a partner along with Tele Danmark in the MiniRuf paging system company.
"The takeover of Talkline means an expansion of Tele Danmark's telephony activities in Germany and Tele Danmark's efforts to integrate fixed and mobile telephone services there," it said.

Talkline is the second biggest service firm in Germany's telecommunications industry, with some 385,000 customers, a seven percent share of the GSM mobile telephone market and sharply rising turnover at 539 million marks in first-half 1996/97.

In Germany, Tele Danmark has a 20 percent share in MiniRuf as well as operating fixed telephony services through its German Tele Danmark Internetz unit which has an interconnect pact with Deutsche Telekom. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
